basis: Universal developmental delay and intellectual disability; language impairment and behavioral abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Clonal histiocytic neoplasm; direct nervous-system infiltration reported in approximately 49% of patients; other organ sites are individually less common.
Terminal complement deficiency is an immunodeficiency; resulting infections are separately diagnosed diseases.
Predominantly ovarian benign epithelial-stromal tumor; reproductive organs have no axis. No covered organ of origin is established here.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss documented in 12/12 patients.
Substance dependence is a psychiatric condition; no direct organ damage is specified.
HSV directly infects and damages brain; hyponatremia, leukocytosis and assisted ventilation do not establish direct injury to additional organs.
Viral infection directly inflames lung parenchyma.
Hirschsprung disease, deafness and polydactyly define the syndrome; renal agenesis 30-79%. ID annotation omitted at cap and conflicts with non-ID parent.
Thyroid hormone transport disorder with defining severe neurologic impairment and muscle hypoplasia/atrophy; hypertension occurs in 30-79%.
Complement-mediated glomerular injury with C3 deposition, hematuria and progressive renal dysfunction.
Umbrella for tick-transmitted infections; no additional organ is consistently damaged across the group.
Inherited right ventricular myocardial degeneration and arrhythmia.
Disease of gingiva and tooth-supporting periodontal tissues; the umbrella includes noninfectious disorders and does not imply generalized skeletal injury.
Idiopathic podocyte injury and glomerular scarring; proposed circulating permeability factors alone do not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Ovarian germ-cell tumor; reproductive organs have no axis, and this is not a hormone-producing endocrine neoplasm.
Acquired thickening of skin; variable underlying causes do not establish a shared additional organ or mechanism axis.
Progressive acquired skin hyperpigmentation without other symptoms or established systemic disease.
Recurrent dislocation of the fibular head is a structural joint disorder.
Cerebrovascular ischemia causes cerebral tissue infarction and persistent focal neurologic deficits.
Enteroviral intercostal and diaphragmatic myositis defines epidemic pleurodynia; pleural inflammation is not sufficiently consistent for a pulmonary label.
Thymic epithelial tumor lies outside the listed axes; it is not a lymphoma. Associated myasthenia, red-cell aplasia and immunodeficiency are separate diseases.
Classic Timothy syndrome combines severe long-QT arrhythmia with neurodevelopmental dysfunction; type 2 lacks cutaneous syndactyly.
Primary immunodeficiency from defective immunoglobulin class switching; infections and subtype-specific complications do not establish shared organ damage.
Anterior segment dysgenesis and characteristic dental hypoplasia define the syndrome; hearing, cardiac and CNS findings lack evidence of frequency above 30%.
